title: Biomechanical assessment of various punching techniques
retraction_or_correction_status: no retraction or correction recorded in OpenAlex at accessed_at
notes: cited_by_count 30 at harvest; a citation count is a measure of attention, not of correctness
methodology: Kistler force plate at 10 kHz with 2 kHz high-speed video; fist, hand-edge and open-hand strikes, dominant and non-dominant, randomised order; force, impulse, impact duration and effective mass.
main_findings: Reports impulse, impact duration and EFFECTIVE MASS alongside peak force - the quantity that separates a fast hand from a heavy one.
Untrained population, which makes it a floor rather than a ceiling for human punch output.
limitations: strikes into a wall-mounted pad, so no opponent motion

quoted_evidence.quote: the effective mass of the punch (the ratio between impulse and velocity)

project_implications: Our impact model derives delivered force from stamina cost. Effective mass and impulse are the measured quantities that would let that be checked against something real rather than internally consistent.
Impact duration is a number we do not model at all and animation currently implies.
